Senses.PreferredTarget: already present and ready at hand
Senses.Explanation: Already present, complete, or ready at hand rather than newly produced. Named Chan speakers apply the word to each encountered matter, a public case, immediate use, scenery before the eyes, and everything disclosed in the present scene. Yuanwu Keqin pairs 'this very thing is ready' with 'this very thing is for use'; Ruibai Mingxue asks who lacks what is originally ready, while Hanxiu Xingyun pairs original completeness with everything already present. Chan bends an ordinary word for something ready-made by using it to challenge the search for a result elsewhere, yet the word itself does not tell the reader what the ready thing is in every passage.
Senses.Note: Canonical concordance: 1,895 exact hits in 315 files and 311 works. Seven distinct deployments across six works. Grammatical shifts do not create different referents.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34 through 120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Zhantang Wenzhun section. Zhantang Wenzhun is the exact speaker saying that the great way runs freely and is ready in each encountered matter.

Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34 through 120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Jingyin Furi Weiyue section. Weiyue is the exact speaker calling it a ready-made public case before the old sail has been hung.
Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄). Yuanwu Keqin is the exact speaker pairing this very thing being ready at hand with this very thing being available for use.
Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ruibai (入就瑞白禪師語錄). Ruibai Mingxue is the exact speaker asking who has no share in what is originally ready at hand.
